publications.title: Mitigasi Ancaman Siber pada Aplikasi Web Melalui SIEM: Tinjauan Literatur Sistematis
publications.abstract: Web applications have become the backbone of the modern digital ecosystem, yet their openness makes them primary targets for cyberattacks that conventional defense mechanisms often fail to detect. This article presents a systematic literature review of 13 selected publications from the Scopus database from the 2020-2025 period to analyze the effectiveness of Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) in mitigating threats to web applications. The review identifies dominant attack categories including SQL Injection (SQLi), Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), and application-layer Denial of Service (DoS) attacks. Research demonstrates that a hybrid approach integrating SIEM with Web Application Firewalls (WAF) and the application of Machine Learning algorithms is proven to detect zero-day attack anomalies with accuracy rates reaching 97% to 100%. Furthermore, the use of open-source platforms such as Wazuh and ELK Stack enables centralized security visibility monitoring and significant reduction in incident response times. This article recommends the adoption of an integrated security architecture combining rule-based and behavioral log analysis to minimize false positive rates and build robust, adaptive web defenses.
publications.source_detail: Jurnal Riset Informatika dan Teknologi Informasi

publications.title: Alternating Methods for Large-Scale AC Optimal Power Flow with Unit Commitment
publications.abstract: Security-constrained unit commitment with alternating current optimal power flow (SCUC-ACOPF) is a central problem in power grid operations that optimizes commitment and dispatch of generators under a physically accurate power transmission model while encouraging robustness against component failures. SCUC-ACOPF requires solving large-scale problems that involve multiple time periods and networks with thousands of buses within strict time limits. In this work, we study a detailed SCUC-ACOPF model with a rich set of features of modern power grids, including price-sensitive load, reserve products, transformer controls, and energy-limited devices. We propose a decomposition scheme and a penalty alternating direction method to find high-quality solutions to this model. Our methodology leverages spatial and temporal decomposition, separating the problem into a set of mixed-integer linear programs for each bus and a set of continuous nonlinear programs for each time period. To improve the performance of the algorithm, we introduce a variety of heuristics, including restrictions of temporal linking constraints, a second-order cone relaxation, and a contingency screening algorithm. We quantify the quality of feasible solutions through a dual bound from a second-order cone program. To evaluate our algorithm, we use large-scale test cases from Challenge 3 of the U.S. Department of Energy s Grid Optimization Competition that resemble real power grid data under a variety of operating conditions and decision horizons. The experiments yield feasible solutions with an average optimality gap of 1.33%, demonstrating that this approach generates near-optimal solutions within stringent time limits.

publications.title: Rancang Bangun Aplikasi Perpustakaan Sekolah Berbasis Android Di SMK Negeri 07 Kota Bengkulu
publications.abstract: Current advancements in information technology are driving the transformation of school library management systems from conventional methods to digital-based systems. To date, SMK Negeri 07 Bengkulu City still employs a manual recording system for managing book collections, member data, and loan/return transactions. This situation carries the risk of recording errors and data loss, while also resulting in low operational efficiency. This study aims to design and develop an Android-based school library application to enhance the effectiveness, efficiency, and accessibility of library management. The system development method employed is the Waterfall model, comprising five key stages: requirements analysis, system design, code implementation, testing, and maintenance. The application was developed using the WebView-based Median.co platform, featuring an interactive web interface optimized for Android mobile devices. Research results indicate that the developed application facilitates book searches, member data recording, and library transactions through a computerized, real-time process. Black-box testing revealed a 100% success rate across all tested functional scenarios. Furthermore, questionnaire data from 32 respondents—analyzed using SPSS via the Pearson Product-Moment correlation test—showed an r-calculated value exceeding the r-table value (0.349) and a p-value of less than 0.001. Consequently, the application is deemed highly suitable, valid, and effective for implementation at SMK Negeri 07 Bengkulu City.
publications.source_detail: Jurnal Riset Informatika dan Teknologi Informasi

publications.title: A.R.E.S. Evidence Companion — Observable AI Interaction-State Divergences
publications.abstract: The A.R.E.S. (Acoustic Resonance Echo System) Evidence Companion documents visible changes in AI replies, interface states, process summaries and reports of tool actions. It separates observations, user reports, displayed model statements, interpretations and open hypotheses. The illustrated reading section follows one October screenshot pair into the detailed case record. The four October pairs come from one connected conversation. The core corpus has a 2 October 2026 intake cutoff, with separately dated November addenda on agent competition and feedback, and reference cues and reported log access. The main text and exhibit commentary are in English. Many of the reproduced excerpts and screenshots retain the original German. This report was developed through human–AI research collaboration involving analysis, structuring and drafting. The collaboration is documented in the report and companion archive. Final review and publication decisions rest with Jessica Schmidt.
publications.source_detail: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

publications.title: Animating microbiology and immunology: student tool preferences and pedagogical insights in an AI era
publications.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools have changed how undergraduate students approach written coursework, often bypassing required levels of active reading and conceptual engagement. To encourage genuine interaction with course content without resorting to high-stress invigilated exams, a low-stakes digital animation task (2% weighting) was integrated into an undergraduate microbiology and immunology course, to pilot students’ preferences on using animation tools to construct visuals. Students created a 30-s animation, illustrating dynamic biological processes, such as viral replication or phagocytosis. Pre- and post-exercise surveys evaluated students’ prior tool experience, selection criteria and software adoption. Pre-survey results showed that only 57% of students had prior animation experience – predominantly using Microsoft PowerPoint (32%). Key tool selection criteria included user-friendliness (32%), available tutorial support (18%) and zero cost (15%). Following targeted tutorial support for in-house digital tools (e.g. Adobe Express, Adobe Animate, Adobe Character Animator) and autonomy to select Adobe or other preferred tools for the task, post-survey analysis demonstrated a substantial rise in preference for Adobe Express, growing from 2 to 41%, while maintaining high levels of student engagement. Tutors observed that translating biological concepts into moving representations required greater time-on-task, research and deconstruction of study content to construct an accurate visual, thus offering an effective, AI-resistant assessment strategy for science education.

publications.title: Bastion: a governed agent fleet for Google Cloud IAM review (source code, v0.9.2)
publications.abstract: Source code of Bastion, a three-agent fleet that reviewed Google Cloud IAM access with deterministic policy authority, explicit agent handoffs and completion confirmations. v0.9.2 is a source-only release and was never deployed; the final deployment, evaluated in the technical report, was v0.9.1. The fleet was retired on 9 November 2026. publications.title: AI IN STYLE
publications.abstract: This mixed-methods study examines how Generation Z consumers interact with generative artificial intelligence (GAI) chatbots in the context of fashion retail. Unlike traditional chatbots, GAI chatbots generate responses dynamically rather than relying on pre-programmed replies, enabling more natural and interactive engagement. Study One explores how consumers use GAI chatbots across hedonic and utilitarian product tasks to satisfy different needs, guided by the Uses and Gratifications (U&G) framework. Data were collected through focus group interviews with 17 participants and analyzed to identify key themes and subthemes. Findings revealed that cognitive, affective, and personal integrative needs were fulfilled through chatbot interaction, while social integrative and tension release needs were not. Personalized responses also emerged as a key factor enhancing the consumer experience. Study Two further investigates chatbot adoption using the U&G framework, with trust modeled as a central mechanism to influence adoption. Data were collected through an online survey, yielding 397 valid responses, and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Results indicate that cognitive needs were the strongest predictor of trust, followed by personalized responses, while affective and tension release needs were not significant. Product type did not significantly influence chatbot trust. These findings suggest that retailers can leverage GAI chatbot tools to enhance customer engagement, deliver personalized shopping experiences, and build trust, ultimately increasing adoption and purchase intention.

publications.title: EDITORIAL VOL. 11 2026 – Evolución tecnológica al servicio de la comunicación científica. MOJP 4.0 y una nueva etapa de desarrollo editorial
publications.abstract: This editorial presents MOJP 4.0, a technological evolution of the editorial infrastructure of the Peer-Reviewed Scientific Journal of the MenteClara Foundation, developed by Oscar R. Gómez and his engineering team on the basis of OJS 3.5.0.5. It describes its main innovations: optimization of the metadata architecture, implementation of interoperable semantic schemas, improved identification of authors and institutions through persistent identifiers, expansion of OAI-PMH services, and integration of XMP metadata into PDF documents. It also presents Custom Head Injector, a native MOJP 4.0 module compatible with OJS 3.5.0.5 and later versions, which expands the possibilities for customizing and integrating metadata, semantic schemas, and external services into the HTML header of editorial platforms. The editorial also introduces the XMP-PDF Module, a technology designed to enrich scientific documents with structured information about their bibliographic identity, editorial provenance, rights, and other relevant data. These developments are part of an institutional trajectory of innovation, technological autonomy, and commitment to the principles of openness, interoperability, and the circulation of scientific information.
publications.source_detail: Revista Científica Arbitrada de la Fundación MenteClara

publications.title: Improving Click-Through Rate for New Content Websites in Google Search: A Practitioner Case Study of Title and Snippet Optimisation
publications.abstract: New content websites often earn search impressions well before they earn clicks. This paper examines that gap using Google Search Console data from NextPlayIntel (nextplayintel.com), a gaming news and deals site covering many games, which received its first Google impression on 24 October 2026. Over a 28-day window, the site recorded 382 clicks from 38,827 impressions, a click-through rate (CTR) under 1%, with most impressions at positions 4–10. A query- and page-level review found four recurring problems: snippets that contradicted searcher intent, titles that went stale after an event, broad queries the site could not win, and image-search impressions that inflated totals. A narrow how-to guide, by contrast, reached 7.2% CTR. Nine titles were rewritten on 11 November 2026. The paper describes each pattern and the interventions, and offers a reusable checklist. The effect of the rewrites has not yet been measured; those results are pending.
publications.source_detail: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

publications.title: Penerapan Microlearning dalam Meningkatkan Literasi Digital dan Kemampuan Pemrograman: Studi Literatur Review
publications.abstract: Microlearning, the delivery of content in small units focused on a single learning goal, is increasingly used to build digital competence, yet evidence on its effects on digital literacy and programming ability has rarely been synthesised together. This study maps intervention characteristics, effectiveness, and implementation challenges. A systematic literature review following PRISMA 2020 covered journal articles, proceedings, and theses from 2016-2026, searched through open academic search on 16 October 2026. Of 48 records assessed, 14 primary studies were included (10 on digital literacy or competence, 4 on programming). All five controlled experimental studies favoured the Microlearning group; pre-post studies without comparison groups showed gains but are weak for causal inference. Recurring features were short single-concept units, interactivity with immediate feedback, and repeated access. Main barriers were infrastructure, teachers’ content-production skills, fragmented attention, and evidence quality. Microlearning appears promising as a complement to, not a replacement for, conventional instruction.
publications.source_detail: BLAZE Jurnal Bahasa dan Sastra dalam Pendidikan Linguistik dan Pengembangan
